Elections roadshow: Limpopo's community takes their town back

By: Sasha Schwendenwein | Production

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We are going to one of the better municipality's, however, that doesn't mean it's good.

Unique Selling Point:
https://www.hoedspruit.co.za/history-of-hoedspruit

What I liked about the Mopane district, is that 4 of its municipalities are shocking, and maruleng is actually okay… however, that doesn’t mean it’s good. And that’s kind of what I want to focus on. We can focus on the worst, but there you’ll find nothing works, so lets look at a place that works, has issues, but we can work around them.

WATER THEME: But just as food security is important, you really can only grow things if you have water. Water is life! But Hoedspruits water is tied up in a municipality deal with the airforce base… So water is bought from the airforce base… and the department of public works often does not pay for it: So they get their water from the Blyde River (cleanest river in the country), however the airforce base are contracted to transport the water from its source (the Blyde river water utility company oversees this)… however without any payment they cannot do this. This happens ALL the time which is why communities are left literally DRY. The airforce base literally put out a message that said the department of public works will have to go fetch the water themselves and deliver it as they hadn’t paid in months. It’s a right to have water, and because of non-payment that is affecting entire areas.

HOUSING THEME: Another issue is a lack of housing for workers in the towns where there are jobs… so the community has a project – where the scotia cattle farm was bought for the community, and they’ve decided to turn into affordable housing for those who work in the areas, otherwise the only options are locations. Some people have taken to living under the towns bridge – which is a railway line, and there have been two fires there killing residents. So housing is a big issue around the province.

BORDER/MOZAM/ZIMBABWE

MINING THEME: I mean Phalaborwa is an hour away and has a place called Mordor which is the centre of the mining industry in the area – a giant phosphate mine that poisoned the river leading into the KNP olifants river. Most towns are so reliant on these mining industries, like Steelpoort, and the Waterberg for coal for Medupi power station.


HLOKOMELA CLINIC Just outside of Hoedspruit is Hlokomela clinic, made for the workers of the surrounding community. It focuses specifically on farm workers – as Limpopo is a major exporter nationally and internationally of its produce – this is important for food security. But we need to have healthy workers. And as there are no hospitals in the area, Hlokomela was born.
Hlokomela is an award winning HIV and AIDS educational and treatment programme targeting workers, including foreign migrants, in the agriculture, nature conservation and tourism sectors in The Greater Kruger to Canyons area located in Limpopo and Mpumalanga. The programme aims to reduce HIV vulnerability through peer education, raising of awareness, prevention and treatment. The project has been running successfully for the past 11 years and is currently rolled out on 71 sub project sites. An estimated 25 000 people are reached annually through the activities of the programme. In 2008 from 29% to 6%, sex workers are on PREP.
Villages in mopane… million missing…water…


LACK OF MUNICIPAL SERVICES: Everything has to be privatized – so there’s a real lack of services around the country, so one project is the “town cleaning project” in which all the residents get together on a Saturday to clean the area…


Summary:
For a province named after a river – Limpopo sure has a lack of water. It’s their biggest concern speaking to the people on the ground. The communities often go days without water, and it’s also a province that goes well into the 40’s during the summer months. This is a problem not only for the communities, but also for the tourism industry as Limpopo is serves the international tourists who come to the Kruger National Park or the Waterberg Biosphere (which is a UNESCO world heritage site). It consists of 5 districts, and 25 local municipalities. Economically is exports are fruit, cotton, sunflowers, maize, peanuts, avo’s, tea and timber plantations (major forestry industries) and has the largest coal deposit in the country. However, with all this wealth it has a big gap between it’s poor and rich residents, even more so in the rural areas. Agriculturally, it’s known beef cattle country as much of it is bushveld. 80% South Africa’s game hunting industry is found here. This all demands water… and again there is none – so all the private people need to have their own boreholes and private water reservoirs, so that means any business or farm or hotel etc but this is not something that the average person can afford, so they really suffer. In the Waterberg this has been a problem for years, their water issues are well documented, however, in places like Hoedspruit the surrounding community lives without water for 4-5 days on average in a week. Another really important issue throughout the province are roads and road maintenance. Lydenbrug for example has potholes the size of cars, but rural locations are also kept rural because of a lack of infrastructure. We know that there is a lack of service delivery throughout the country and that isn’t any different than in Limpopo. The AGs 2020 report shows this province has the same issues as any other, so I actually want to focus on the differences here. Not the similarities.

Further information:
HISTORY:
Polokwane, Limpopo - People in this province care about its borders, land and farming, tourism, water, education and housing. Because...well its the game hunting captial of South Africa, as the kruger is there, as well as the waterburg its a big tourist destination. Its known for farming fruit like grapes and avocadoes and has many tea/coffee plantations. It also has a sizable forresty industry. Its mining industry is massive (phosphates and coal) in terms of places like steelpoort. It has the largest platinum deposit in the country. Education: it has mostly TVET colleges, but also the famous limpopo univeristy. It has a white elephant called the Peter Mokaba stadium. It's just really updated its road system, especially around Polokwane. And the housing in urban areas HAS BLOOMED. It's known for potholes! Heat! And the ZCC church! Moria is the base for the ZCC church and during easter and there are between 11-15 million members nationally. It has a large young black population and needs to focus on internet connectivity as much of it is rural. Provincial Address by Premier: https://www.gov.za/speeches/premier-chupu-mathabatha-limpopo-state-province-address-20212022-25-feb-2021-0000#:~:text=Premier%20Chupu%20Mathabatha%3A%20Limpopo%20State,2021%2F2022%20%7C%20South%20African%20Government their examples of successful youth: Ms Mahlako Kgamedi uses her Facebook block and YouTube account for progressive social commentary. This young lady from Sekhukhune District enjoys the following of over 60 thousand of her social media accounts. She has already secured several corporate endorsements for her online popularity. Another one is a young man Ntebatse Segodiso is a young man from Bolobedu in Mopani District who had developed a ride-hailing application. His app is called Pick-Up. The app is designed to allow users to request a ride through their mobile devices. This has allowed several young people to earn an income as Pick-Up drivers.

Jonas Lekganyane is the brains behind the much-loved Adventures of Noko Mashaba animated series. Mr Lekganyane grew up in the dusty villages of Mankweng in the Capricorn District. This youngster has turned his hobby into a serious business and he is now collaborating some of Africa’s biggest brands. "We have set aside an amount of R3.5 billion to augment the available resources to drive our response. A large sum of this allocation will go to the social cluster, which include health, education and social development. This is in line with the caring and social content of our response. Human development and the wellbeing of our people are essential.

From the R3.5 billion, we have allocated R500 million to support enterprise development, farmer support and road infrastructure." The tourism sector in Limpopo held poll position countrywide in domestic travels with approximately 22.2 million arrivals. We have secured assistance to 294 tourism establishment from the National Tourism Relief Fund, to the tune of R14.7 million. We supplemented this amount with R10 million to cater for those not covered by the National Tourism Relief Fund.

Limpopo is largely a rural province with vast arable lands. It is in this context that we welcome the initiative led by the Minister of Agriculture, Land Reform and Rural Development, Honourable Thoko Didiza, to allocate state land on a lease basis. This land allocation will go a long way towards transforming and expanding productive capacity of the sector.
In Limpopo, approximately 122 thousand hectares of state land is earmarked for this process. We are confident that young people, woFor us to breathe life into our struggling economy, we need a focussed investment in infrastructure. Ending the legacy of unequal development is our priority. Our goal is to upgrade rural areas through equitable distribution of development and investment to bring them on par with developed areas. men and people living with disabilities will be among the beneficiaries. Currently, Trans-Caledon Tunnel Authority is exploring funding options with the DBSA to facilitate implementation of Phase 2B of the Olifants River Water Resources Development Project. This project consists of a 70 kilometre pipeline from Flag Boshielo Dam to Pruisen near Mokopane. Upon completion, this project will augment water supply for the surrounding mines and provide additional water for domestic users.

We are at the design phase of the Olifants River Water Resources Development Project. This project comprises a pipeline of raw water from Steelpoort pump station to Ga-Mathipa Reservoir, a balancing dam, pump station; and steel pipeline from Ga-Mathipa pump station to the existing Mooihoek Water Treatment Works.

Script:


Collecting rainwater or sourcing it from mountain streams isn’t unusual for 71 Year old small scale farmer Katherine Komane.
In my life I am crying for water.
Katherine’s mother, Nora Elizabeth Sethla, still helps out with the housework despite her 101 years.
upsound singing
It’s a quiet existence. The remoteness of their village means their concerns often go unheard in the build up to municipal elections. Yet the issues affecting the lives of people in Turkey, in Limpopo’s Mopani District, mirror those in towns and villages across the province of 6 million people.
What I really want is that the municipality can assist me with a borehole.
If she wants her complaints heard, her nearest municipality – Maruleng - is an hour away by taxi and costs R60 one-way.
Since I started voting from 1994 I have not seen any improvement in my life, even the water tank they are bringing to the community we are not receiving most of us. It goes to those they know.
It might be named after a river, but for limpopo residents and its 5 districts, water or metsi is a luxury.
LINK: ACCORDING TO THE AUDITOR GENERAL, THAT’S THE RESULT OF MALADMINISTRATION AND CORRUPTION. OF THE 22 LOCAL MUNICIPALITIES, NONE ARE STABLE AND MOST ARE CONSIDERED CLOSE TO DYSFUNCTIONAL.
Maruleng is in Hoedspruit, bordering Mpumalanga and its tourist drawcard, the Kruger Park.
UPSOUND: I’m Chris Turner of Hoedspruit FM…
Hoedspruit Radio presenter Chris Turner retired here in 2006.
We have a population of over 100000 people within the municipality, and we probably only have about two thousand people paying the rates.
Hoedspruit is Limpopo’s economic hub. This district has 3 main sources of income and employment: mining, farming and tourism. All of these sectors need LOTS of water.
The water that comes out the taps is not very good. So there are a number of companies locally that supply bottled water for drinking, and a lot of people are installing their own filtered filtration. None of the villages around here have a decent water supply. So a lot of the workers, a lot of people who come to town don't have a proper water supply at home.
In this area, Civil society organizations like AWARD have stepped up to assist the municipality. Its Deputy Director is Derick du Toit.
Award is the Association for Water and Rural Development, water becomes fundamental in terms of breaking into the economy. because we've got the legacy of so many Bantustans former homelands that literally have still lagged behind on the development kind of profile. So they have never been integrated into the commercial formal sector.
Led by Isaac Malajie, residents in the Turkey community contributed towards this borehole. But it was AWARD and a partner organization that installed it to help 13 farmers.
Isaac:Those are the farmers who contributed money towards the borehole and have access to it .
Small-scale farmer Komane has used traditional farming methods for 20 years, but now relies on water saving and organic techniques.
KK: they taught me on how to farmer sustainable, things like mulching, adding chicken and cow compost . We don’t use synthetic fertilizers at all
But then covid struck and her income vanished. So AWARD came up with a plan B.
So we designed what was called the Talle Table Network, So this is a tablecloth and the tuble table literally means green table. And so this is a network of green tables,
These merchants go to public events in their villages, and sell produce on these tablecloths so the community knows it's locally sourced.
KK: per month I make about R300-00 from my garden
Bigboy Mkhabela believes AWARD has embraced Limpopo’s spirit with this project.
Each and every household has its own mango tree, pawpaw tree or any kind of there in your back garden, because we don’t believe in putting money and buying all the time.
Many workers employed in Hoedspruit travel 45 minutes into town from it’s nearest village, Acornhoek – on the Mpumalanga border.
There isn't any land for people working in town. So we end up with we have an informal squatter, a squatter camp, we have a formal squatter camp just on the other side of town, but they're not provided with facilities. There's no ablutions, refuse collection is non-existent and you can't blame the people they work in town.
In the past 20 years we have vote but nothing changed, still the same with the roads, even now we are going potholes on top of potholes, this standing pipe has got 5 years, no water is coming out.
The potholes and that’s how I got damage on my car, it’s going to R3000-R4000
He can’t do much about the roads but Art Teacher Walter Sibuyi has been beautifying his local high school with paintings of the surrounding nature.
Im teaching the subject of visual art because without it, there is no life.
His family was forcibly removed from Hoedspruit during apartheid, but he’s been passing on his love of nature to his students. Many of them have loved ones caught up in the scourge of poaching - which the children recognize discourages tourists from visiting the area.
You see the guests. They are moving away because they want won't see any rhino and the person who killed in the line is saying that is a useless person who is educated. You don't know what is going to use with this money, only to buy liquor.
A lack of access to affordable housing and land is another major issue here. Those lucky enough to have successfully claimed land look to AWARD for assistance.
LINK: MARULENG MUNICIPALITY HAS SPENT OVER A QUARTER OF A BILLION RAND ON (R276 MILLION) SETTLING LAND CLAIMS, BUT HAS ONLY MANAGED TO CONCLUDE 5 OR THE 21 CLAIMS LODGED. AND LIKE MANY OTHER PARTS OF THE COUNTRY, ONCE THE CLAIM HAS BEEN ACCEPTED AND SETTLED, ENSURING THE LAND REMAINS PRODUCTIVE IS A MAJOR CHALLENGE.
But award they are what they taught us. A lot of things like the beneficiation. .
Derick Thobejane lives in one of 6 communities awarded 19,500 hectres inside the Lekgalametsi Nature Reserve.
Financially, it's viable because people come here and get jobs here, but we want to develop this place into a into a tourist destination.
AWARD and its project partners boosted the local community’s financial and management skills.
that they can actually have managerial skills in managing what is now their park
I believe that the development is what is in your head. You can have more in bricks, but if you cannot use them properly or you think outside the box, the buildings would be useless.
LINK: WHILE MARULENG MUNICIPALITY PROVIDES FOR HEALTH CARE IN ITS INTEGRATED DEVELOPMENT PLAN, THE HEALTH OF FARM WORKERS HAS LARGELY BEEN FORGOTTEN. ASTONISHING WHEN YOU CONSIDER THEY MAKE UP 10% OF THE PROVINCE’S WORKFORCE.
It’s a gap filled by Hlokomela Clinic… the brainchild of Nurse Christine du Preez. Amongst their patient cohort, HIV rates in farm workers have plummeted from 29 to 6 percent in just 16 years.
You get your chronic medication every month. We have a women's clinic and we do ultrasounds and pap smears. We have a sex workers program.
Citrus farmer Lohanzi Jansen van vuren has much to thank Hlokolema for.
There was a lot of stigma going around and Hlokomela because a lot of people thought they would lose their jobs...if they tested positive.
Farm worker Constance Ngobeni was taken advantage of sexually by past supervisors. She’s now much more familiar with her rights thanks to Hlokomela clinic.
it was terrible before if we want job, supervisors said that if you cannot love me you can never get work.
Hlokomela has helped keep her gainfully employed and healthy.
If you’re not healthy you get treatment and go back to work.
people became more open about going to hlokomela and saying I have an appointment and going to fetch ARVs
This has helped the productivity of the farms…
If you get a sick letter from hlokomela then its for good reason why they’re not at the work place.
With elections on the horizon, Maruleng has told the community it is addressing service delivery issues and this month bought land it’s hoped will be used to provide affordable housing. Time will tell whether this is an election issue eventually delivered on or another broken promise.
They only promise us when there’s votes, but then after votes, then they forget.

metadata.Summary: For a province named after a river – Limpopo sure has a lack of water. It’s their biggest concern speaking to the people on the ground. The communities often go days without water, and it’s also a province that goes well into the 40’s during the summer months. This is a problem not only for the communities, but also for the tourism industry as Limpopo is serves the international tourists who come to the Kruger National Park or the Waterberg Biosphere (which is a UNESCO world heritage site). It consists of 5 districts, and 25 local municipalities. Economically is exports are fruit, cotton, sunflowers, maize, peanuts, avo’s, tea and timber plantations (major forestry industries) and has the largest coal deposit in the country. However, with all this wealth it has a big gap between it’s poor and rich residents, even more so in the rural areas. Agriculturally, it’s known beef cattle country as much of it is bushveld. 80% South Africa’s game hunting industry is found here. This all demands water… and again there is none – so all the private people need to have their own boreholes and private water reservoirs, so that means any business or farm or hotel etc but this is not something that the average person can afford, so they really suffer. In the Waterberg this has been a problem for years, their water issues are well documented, however, in places like Hoedspruit the surrounding community lives without water for 4-5 days on average in a week. Another really important issue throughout the province are roads and road maintenance. Lydenbrug for example has potholes the size of cars, but rural locations are also kept rural because of a lack of infrastructure. We know that there is a lack of service delivery throughout the country and that isn’t any different than in Limpopo. The AGs 2020 report shows this province has the same issues as any other, so I actually want to focus on the differences here. Not the similarities.
